title: What If US Treasuries Rebound?
gist: Louis-Vincent Gave notes long-dated US Treasuries failed to rebound at quarter-end despite weak payrolls and rebalancing flows, with the long-bond ETF's 14-day RSI at 14.9, and asks what happens if they do rebound.

insights.claim: Long-dated US Treasuries showed no quarter-end rebound despite a decent equity quarter, weak non-farm payrolls, disappointing China growth and French political trouble, all of which would normally support bonds.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Absence of a bid despite supportive catalysts signals structural selling pressure.

insights.claim: The 14-day RSI on the long-dated bond ETF hit 14.9, an extreme oversold reading reflecting low regard for long Treasuries after an ugly quarter, year, three, five and ten years.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Oversold extremes set up a possible tactical rebound; the question the piece poses.

insights.claim: The bearish case for Treasuries is obvious: runaway deficits, wars, weaponization of the dollar and Treasury market, and protectionism.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Structural drivers of long-end weakness remain.
